clue.text: South American rebel group's means of avoiding duty

parts.note: the Contras were rebels fighting Nicaragua's Sandinista government in the 1980s
a band is a group, here of musicians; the 's is a link meaning 'has'

explanation.surface: A Latin American guerrilla outfit is credited with a clever way of dodging taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: smuggled goods are what pass without customs duty being paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Smuggled goods are brought in precisely so that customs charges are evaded, so they are a way of escaping tax.

clue.text: Secret stores church found in case, possibly

indicators.note: the church abbreviation is placed inside the rearranged word, as something found within it
possibly signals that the word case may appear in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Hidden hoards belonging to a church turn up inside a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like part of the picture, a box, but it is the fodder; 'possibly' scrambles it to CAES before 'found in' does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural noun for hidden hoards, such as stockpiles of food or weapons concealed somewhere.

clue.text: Drop off family item used at table

parts.note: to drop off is to fall asleep briefly, to nap
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: A household object is put down at the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth or paper square for wiping fingers and lips is a standard piece of dining equipment.

clue.text: Show surprise seeing one bare wire, say, frayed

indicators.note: a frayed wire has its strands unravelled and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is startled at the sight of an exposed, worn electrical cable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting one brow is the idiomatic facial gesture of mild astonishment or scepticism.

clue.text: Setter's barking following bend in London road

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the word for bend

parts.note: to bow is to bend the body forward

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of setter go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter, a breed of gun dog, is yapping as its owner turns a corner on a street in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' looks like the dog's noise but means crazy, rearranging SETTER into STREET; the 's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A street in Covent Garden, famous for its magistrates' court and the Bow Street Runners, an early police force.

clue.text: Direction taken by prime minister once

definitions.meaning: one of the four compass points
Lord ... was British prime minister from 1770 to 1782, during the American War of Independence

explanation.surface: A former premier is said to have adopted a particular course.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a compass bearing and the title of the eighteenth-century premier Lord North.

clue.text: Useful quality dismissing the good in adverts

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: plugs are pieces of promotion, adverts for something
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Something worthwhile is lost when advertising throws out the virtuous stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage or asset is a point in favour, an informal noun sense.

clue.text: Illusionist's look for mother — a straight-thinking individual

indicators.note: for here means one thing put in place of another, so the word for look replaces the word for mother

parts.note: an illusionist is a magician; the 's is a link meaning 'has'
MA is an informal word for mother
LO is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: A conjuror swaps a glance for his mum and turns out to be a clear thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person skilled in formal reasoning thinks in a rigorous, orderly way.

clue.text: Flipping salesmen around famous hotel for a drink

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the hotel name
flipping turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London

explanation.surface: Annoying sales staff are milling about a grand hotel in search of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British curse but signals the turnaround, giving SPER, which is split to go 'around' the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A long drink of white wine mixed with soda water.

clue.text: Gather men tipsy after party spirit — such a spoilsport

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the party and spirit

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
gin is a spirit

indicators.note: tipsy means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Men rounded up and drunk after a party with spirits make a killjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: From Aesop: a dog lying in a manger stops the ox eating hay it cannot eat itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names someone who denies others something they have no use for themselves, a mean-spirited killjoy.

clue.text: Island on which corn may be planted to make a sign?

parts.words: on which corn may be planted to make a sign?
parts.note: adding corn after the island's name gives the goat sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone imagines farming a Mediterranean isle to produce a symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: Put CORN on the end of the island and you get CAPRICORN, a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky island in the Bay of Naples, long a celebrated holiday spot.

clue.text: Militant type working to be accepted by friendly German

indicators.note: being accepted means taken inside, so the word for working goes in

parts.note: warm means friendly and welcoming
on means working, as a machine is switched on

explanation.surface: An aggressive figure who is employed gets welcomed by an amiable man from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who agitates for armed conflict is belligerent, a militant sort.

clue.text: Demanding information contained in Exodus

indicators.note: the word for information is held inside the other word

parts.note: an exodus is a mass departure, an exit
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Insisting on details found in the second book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exodus' looks like the Bible book but means a way out; GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal adjective for pressing or urgent, requiring much effort or attention.

clue.text: Prune topping for this?

parts.note: prune is a verb, to trim, and the topping is the hair on one's head, not a dessert garnish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prune topping' suggests a dessert garnish; read prune as a verb and the topping as the hair on one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimming the hair on top of the head is exactly what a barber's appointment delivers.

clue.text: Refreshment outlet for surfers

parts.note: the surfers browse the web rather than ride waves, and the outlet sells coffee

explanation.walkthrough: 'surfers' suggests a beach kiosk, but here they browse the web.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee shop offering computers for web access serves drinks to those online.

clue.text: Flower of youth reflected?

definitions.meaning: a genus of spring bulbs including daffodils
in Greek myth a beautiful young man fell in love with his own reflection in a pool

explanation.surface: A blossom stands for the young looking back on themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower of youth' reads as one phrase meaning the prime of life; split it after 'Flower'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both the daffodil genus and the youth of myth who was turned into that flower.

clue.text: Not working — the listener's certainly at sea

parts.note: off means not functioning, switched off

indicators.note: what the listener hears is a word that sounds like another, said aloud

parts.note: sure means certainly, as in 'sure, I'll come'

explanation.surface: Someone off duty, as one who hears it is convinced, is out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: In some accents 'sure' is said like SHORE, giving the sound match.
explanation.definitionFit: Located out on the water away from the coast, as of an oil rig or wind farm.

clue.text: Copy one Greek letter inscribed in tile

indicators.note: inscribed means written into, so these letters go inside the tile

parts.note: a slate is a roofing tile
I is the Roman numeral for one
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A single Greek character is carved onto a tile as a reproduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate or mimic something, reproducing its appearance or behaviour.

clue.text: Just southern right-wingers will welcome the end of party lies

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: just means fair
Tories are members of the UK's right-wing Conservative Party

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Fair-minded southern Conservatives will embrace a party's final untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of party' gives Y, which goes in after FAIR, before STORIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanciful tales of magic are a euphemism for untruths, as in telling stories.

clue.text: International wearing right dress for an Italian resort

indicators.note: something wearing clothes has them around it, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: a mini is a short dress

explanation.surface: A global figure picks the correct outfit for a trip to an Italian beach town.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town on the Adriatic coast of Italy, famous for its beach holidays.

clue.text: Physical consequence, being let out in fast car?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the car's name

parts.note: a Jag is a Jaguar, a fast car

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being released in a sports car has bodily effects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns LET into ETL, which goes into JAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiredness after crossing time zones is a bodily after-effect of air travel.

clue.text: Sleep in ghetto and live rough at first

parts.note: a slum is a run-down urban district, like a ghetto
to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Getting some rest in a poor district and living rough.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning a state of rest, or a verb meaning to doze; both match.

clue.text: Creature in love depressed by Redditch's surroundings

indicators.note: in a down clue, being depressed puts these letters below the town's outer letters
the surroundings of a word are its outer letters, the first and last

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An animal in love is made gloomy by the environs of a Worcestershire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Redditch is a town in Worcestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A large thick-skinned horned animal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Think this person should join game played outside at home

parts.note: the setter's 'this person' means me, the letter I

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the word for at home
played means the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone reckons they should take part in a match played away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' turns GAME into MAGE, which goes outside IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something in the mind, or suppose, as in 'I imagine so'.

clue.text: Musical works coming from speaker with single thus reversed

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

indicators.note: reversed means the word is read backwards

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: Compositions emerge from a speaker with a single record played backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-scale sacred compositions for voices and orchestra, like Handel's Messiah, are musical pieces.

clue.text: Restaurant that has bars

definitions.meaning: a ... or ... room is a restaurant serving ... food
a gridiron of metal bars, or a grating over a window

explanation.surface: An eatery that also serves drinks at its counters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both an eatery specialising in grilled food and a grating made of parallel metal rods.

clue.text: Regular form of rugby with no wingers

indicators.note: wingers are the players on the edges, so the outer letters are dropped

parts.note: sevens is rugby played with seven players a side

explanation.surface: A standard version of rugby is played without wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingers' are rugby positions on the flanks; here they are the word's end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth and uniform, as in an even pace or a steady rhythm.

clue.text: Saving argument against being of use

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
serving means being useful, as in serving a purpose

explanation.surface: A case against thrift that holds it to be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserving or protecting something from waste or loss, a synonym for keeping.
